stances.claim: CJP's greatest accolades for CJ Puno come precisely from the fact that he sometimes disagrees with him but is always 'convinced of the nobility of his intentions, the clarity of his thought and the inevitability of his logic.' This is the most intellectually honest tribute formula in the corpus: admiration grounded in principled disagreement rather than habitual agreement.

stances.claim: The Puno Constitution quotation -- 'The Constitution is the refuge not only of the worthy, but also of the worthless; it is the fortress not only of the strong, but also of the weak' -- is the governing statement of the living-Constitution philosophy that CJP, Puno, Davide and Sereno all share: the Constitution is most important when it protects those least able to protect themselves.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered July 21, 2008 as a testimonial toast at an ALA event for CJ Reynato S. Puno -- following his proclamation as the UP Alumni Association's Most Distinguished Alumnus during the UP centenary; CJP had proposed the ALA testimonial at the last ALA meeting and it was unanimously agreed -- this address by CJP opens by concurring with the 'Shakespeare of the Supreme Court' title but noting that Puno actually excels the English bard: 'Was it not Shakespeare who wrote, The first thing we do is to kill all lawyers?' He offers four Puno quotations as evidence: (1) 'UP taught us that on crucial issues, a UP alumnus has no right to be wrong'; (2) 'The Constitution is the refuge not only of the worthy, but also of the worthless; it is the fortress not only of the strong, but also of the weak'; (3) 'This country does not belong to the powerful. Nor does it belong to the greedy. It belongs to the Filipino whose spirit calls for honesty, for fairness, for justice, for liberty and for prosperity'; (4) in Filipino at Rizal's birthday in Calamba: 'ang kapayapaan ay hindi lamang ang kawalan ng dumadagundong na digmaan. Ito rin ay nakasalalay sa pagkakaroon ng katarungan sa lipunan' -- making Puno 'not only a Shakespeare; he is also a Balagtas.' Before 1995, CJP knew Puno only as 'a distant star'; since joining the SC, intimately. In his 1997 book 'Justice and Faith': 'Like a trained surgeon, he uses his pen with laser-like precision to separate and excise fabrication from truth and pretension from reality... Daring, gutsy and erudite, he oftentimes wages lonely battles against conventional wisdom.' In oral arguments, 'he is at once the terror of lawyers but the authority for his colleagues.' CJP's governing tribute principle: 'the greatest accolades to Chief Justice Puno come not from those who always agree with him, but from those who, from time to time, disagree with him honestly and sincerely but are convinced of the nobility of his intentions, the clarity of his thought and the inevitability of his logic.'
